what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Ask the sources we quote to sign that we represent them fairly: cheaper than every reader checking.
sections.para: Checking that an article represents its sources falls on every reader, at hours of work or many tokens. The source is best placed to judge: ask them, let them add a caveat, and let them sign with a key their website vouches for. Pay them where an article earns money. Most pieces exist; federation between organisations does not yet.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines: the cost of checking, the source as judge, one signature, payment, what exists, readers too.
sections.para: Readers bear the cost of checking sources, repeatedly and without the best context. The source should check instead, add a caveat and sign. One signature replaces many checks. Pay sources where the article earns money. The Pen, signed notes, the key register and domain proofs exist; organisation federation is a proposal; readers can sign their reviews too.

sections.label: Who checks the references?
sections.line: Summaries are where sources get misrepresented, and today only a reader who checks every reference can tell.
sections.para: Articles quote and summarise papers, notices and statements, and summaries drop caveats or take numbers out of context. To be sure, a domain expert or an agent must load the article and every reference and map them, at hours of time or many tokens, repeated per reader, by someone who is not the best judge.

sections.label: The source is the best person to judge
sections.line: Send the source the passage with its hash and links; they agree, disagree or add a caveat, and sign.
sections.para: The author knows what they meant and which caveat matters. The newsroom sends the passage, its hash and its links, asking whether it is a fair representation. The source can agree, disagree or add the caveat that makes it correct, such as 70% but only of these, then signs it with their own key.

sections.label: Why the economics work
sections.line: Checking once at the source beats checking per reader; it can be paid, as some journals pay reviewers.
sections.para: Downstream checking is repeated by every reader rebuilding context; checking at the source is done once by someone who has it, after which readers check one signature and the signer's standing. It puts private corrections on the record. Biology Open pays reviewers £220. The site's economics pages describe paid fact-certifiers, as designs, not services.

sections.label: Keys that a website vouches for
sections.line: pki.sgit.ai proves domains and keys and signs readers in; federation between organisations is not built.
sections.para: pki.sgit.ai keeps a register of people's keys, anchored on mine, with domain proofs via a well-known file, DNS TXT or a gist, two-way links and chains to a pinned root, and sign-in with a key since 24 October. My memo said federation was its latest work; it is not, and remains a proposal. The register holds one real key.

sections.label: Readers go on the record too
sections.line: Readers and researchers sign their own notes with the Pen; Ask cites passages; together, a web of trust.
sections.para: Every article's Pen keeps marks and sends notes with their passage, signed by a browser key the register vouches for and checked from a pinned root. The Ask pane answers only from cited passages on this site. Sources signing their representation and readers signing their views make a web of trust that agents can weigh.

sections.label: Start small
sections.line: Start with individuals, then companies, with rules: ask first, publish caveats as written, signatures cover representation.
sections.para: Start with people we write about who have a domain or GitHub account, then companies needing a website-vouched key. Show the exact passage, hash and links; publish the source's caveat in their words; record refusals without inference; and remember a signature attests a fair summary, not that the claim itself is true.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nobody has signed yet, federation is unbuilt, the register is small, and sources have interests.
sections.para: This is a proposal; no source has reviewed an article through it. Organisation federation is designed, not shipped. The register held one real person key and two agent keys on 24 October. The economic case is an argument, not a measured cost, and a source may sign a flattering summary.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: My memo, corrected; pki.sgit.ai's releases, how-to, sign-in articles and roadmap; this site's v0.13.64.
sections.para: My voice memo of 24 October, corrected where the record differs; pki.sgit.ai's release history to v0.2.28, its how-to page, two sign-in articles, roadmap and directory; this site's v0.13.64 release; and related articles on the Pen, signed opinions, reviews, PKI, bylines and the economics pages.
